newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - January 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - January 1.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government has assured foreign investors that it would continue to protect and promote foreign investment.

- The United States emerged as the top buyer of Pakistani products during 1995-96, accounting for 15.5 percent of total exports which stood at $8.7 billion, some seven percent more than the previous year.
- The rupee fell 17.14 percent against the dollar in 1996.

- The government is holding a special cabinet meeting today to introduce three ordinances to abolish the Pakistan Banking Council, offer more autonomy to the State (central) Bank of Pakistan and initiate banking sector reforms.
- The tribals living in Federally Administered Tribal Area, bordering Afghanistan, have decided that women would not be allowed to cast their votes in the February 3 general elections.
- Two Shi'ite leaders and four others were shot dead by unidentified assailants in two different incidents in Lahore and Multan.
- The caretaker government has referred 43 cases of corruption and misuse of authority against politicians, senior bureaucrats and other people for accountability.
- The World Bank has agreed to transfer all the Trust Funds to Pakistan from January 1, 1997.
- The government is considering a proposal to allow cotton import from India.
- Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd has managed to arrange a short-term loan of $50 million from ABN Amro and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
